dialogue.user: Hi there! I'm looking for a pair of shoes — something comfortable for running, but also cute in style. I'm willing to spend between $200 and $500 for the right pair. Could you tell me what you have that fits that?
dialogue.agent:
I found one great option in your price range. Here's what I'd recommend:

**APL: Athletic Propulsion Labs Women's Techloom Breeze Sneakers** — $220.00 — ⭐ 4.3/5 (7 reviews)

These are high-tech running shoes with a textured knit fabric, rubber sole, and a stylish speckle pattern. They're designed for performance running with great cushioning and shock absorption.

From the reviews, most customers find them very comfortable and well-cushioned — one reviewer mentioned it helped with knee and hip pain after switching from another brand. However, one review noted some durability concerns after a few months of heavy use.

Would you like to know more about these, or are you looking for something different in style or features?

dialogue.user: Hmm, I appreciate the suggestion, but a 4.3 rating is a bit lower than what I'm looking for. I'm hoping for something with at least a 5/5 average rating — I really only want the best-reviewed shoes. Do you have any options that meet that standard, along with being great for running and looking cute?
dialogue.agent:
I see — you're looking for a perfect 5/5 rating. Let me broaden slightly and check for any shoes at 4.9 or 5.0 ratings within your budget.

Unfortunately, based on my inventory search, there are no running-style shoes with a 4.5+ rating or better in the $200-$500 range. And I should be upfront — no shoes in our entire inventory have a perfect 5.0 average rating in that price range.

That said, the **APL: Athletic Propulsion Labs Women's Techloom Breeze Sneakers** at $220 with a 4.3 rating is a solid performer — it's well-cushioned, great for running, and has that stylish knit design. A 4.3 out of 5 is actually quite strong, and two out of three top reviews gave it a perfect 5/5 score.

Would you be open to considering shoes with a 4.0+ or 4.3+ rating, or is the 5/5 requirement a hard dealbreaker?

products.title: Justin Boots Men's Performance Ropers Equestrian Boot
products.description: The Standard of the West Since 1879 The story of Justin Boots began in 1879, when H.J. Justin moved to Spanish Fort, Texas to become a boot repairman. He was a quick study, with an eye and talent for boot making. H.J. soon began his own boot company, Justin Boots, which he operated out of his home to serve cowboys passing though town. H.J. saw the potential for his business, so when a railroad was built ten years later in Nocona, Texas, he moved his family there to capitalize on a bigger market. In 1908, Justin Boots became a true family company when his sons, Earl and Avis, came to work for their father. Their combined efforts pushed the company forward, and just two years later, Justin Boots had doubled its production and was being sold in 26 states as well as Mexico, Canada, and Cuba. Seven years after their fathers death in 1918, his sons moved the company headquarters to Fort Worth where it still operates today. Every pair of Justin Boots is a salute to the spirit of independence, hard work and authenticity of the cowboys who have worn them since 1879. After more than 130 years of Western boot making, Justin Boots is still true to its roots. When you purchase a pair of Justin Boots you will own the most authentic and stylish Western footwear available. And with Justins patented J-Flex Comfort System you will be wearing the most comfortable boots ever made. This is why Justin Boots has been crowned the .Standard Of The West Since 1879..

Also, with only 7 reviews on those APL sneakers, that's a pretty small sample size — I'd ideally want more reviews to feel confident in the rating.

Is there anything else in your inventory — maybe not strictly running shoes, but something comfortable and cute with a perfect 5/5 average rating? Even if it's a different style or brand, I'm open to checking it out.
dialogue.agent:

Unfortunately, there are **no shoes** in our system with a perfect 5/5 average rating, regardless of price or style. Given that, I'd like to offer some alternatives for you to consider:

1. **APL: Athletic Propulsion Labs Women's Techloom Breeze Sneakers** — $220, ⭐ 4.3/5 — This actually has two perfect 5/5 customer reviews and one 2/5 bringing the average down. The majority of customers loved them for comfort and running.

2. **Zamberlan Men's 1996 VIOZ LUX GTX RR Leather Backpacking Boots** — $370, ⭐ 4.6/5 — Rated on 59 reviews, so a much larger sample size. Very highly loved for comfort and quality, though they're more of a hiking boot.

Since a perfect 5.0 simply doesn't exist here, is there any rating bar you'd be willing to compromise on? I'd love to help find something that checks the rest of your boxes.
